The ending feels entirely natural and earned because it brings Martin's internal character arc to a quiet, poignant resolution. Throughout the story, Martin is characterized by his emotional distance, stubbornness, and need to project competence—traits that have strained his relationships with his ex-wife and his son, Daniel. Earlier in the story, after a tense phone call with Daniel the previous night, it is noted that "each had waited for the other to become a different person." 

Sitting with the deceased woman forces Martin to confront mortality, loneliness, and his habit of needing to be "right" rather than gentle or vulnerable. By the time the rescue workers arrive and take over, Martin has undergone a subtle shift. When he calls his son at the very end, simply saying "I’m here" and acknowledging "Yes... I did [call you]," he is finally bridging the emotional gap between them. Ending on the line "Martin waited" directly mirrors his earlier standoffishness with Daniel, showing that he is now willing to wait patiently for connection rather than out of stubborn pride. It is the exact emotional moment the entire piece was leading toward.
